_README: Published Super Two cutoffs, entered by hand. This is to super_two.py
what data/reference_service_time.json is to the service-time math: the
only check that does not come from this project's own data.
WHY IT MATTERS HERE PARTICULARLY: the computed cutoffs land in the
2.11-2.14 band with no tuning, which looks like confirmation and is
not. Every serious bug in this project so far has been a plausible
belief about MLB's rules, encoded, wrong -- and a number that lands
where you expected is exactly how those survived. A published figure
is the only thing that can actually settle it.
WHERE TO FIND THEM: MLB Trade Rumors reports the cutoff each
offseason, usually in a post titled something like 'Super Two Cutoff
Set At X'. Enter it exactly as published, e.g. "2.132".
`season` is the season the class finished, NOT the offseason label. A
cutoff reported in November 2025 for the 2025-26 arbitration class has
season 2025 here.
Rows with `published` left null are skipped, so partial completion is
fine. `ours` is filled in by the validator at run time and is not
input -- do not paste computed values into `published`, that would
make the check vacuous.

ENTERED 2026-10-26, seasons 2021-2025. The season/offseason labelling is the one thing to get right and search summaries get it wrong: several described an article dated 2024/11 as being 'for the 2025 season'. The URL date is the evidence -- the figure is posted in November for the class that has just finished that season -- and each report's own 'up from'/'down from' claim corroborates its neighbour, so the five form a chain rather than five independent guesses.

source: MLB Trade Rumors / Associated Press, offseason report
note: Reported November 2025 (ESPN and AP, 34 Super Twos; Matt McLain last above the line). MLBTR had trailed it at 2.140 in mlbtraderumors.com/2025/10/super-two-cutoff-expected-to-be-around-2-140-years-of-service.html; the November figure is the official one.
